review.title: Candidate failover policy
review.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel of 1, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** is left wide on purpose -- this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, they share an owner, and narrowing it would buy nothing. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so packages/media-engine/** alone means exactly one of this task, PL-0206 and PL-0205's successor PL-0207 can be active at a time. That is a PATH fact and not a capacity one, and the distinction matters now: claude-media's maxParallel was raised from 1 to 2 in round 40, which changes nothing here because these three still share real files, and was done for PL-0601, whose surface is disjoint from all of them. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0.
review.acceptance: Retry and fallback behavior is bounded, deterministic, observable, and testable

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck via npm run check, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree this gate is recorded against.

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0 on the tree this gate is recorded against: fifty-nine unit cases in failover.test.ts plus sixteen properties in failover.property.test.ts and twelve in scheduling.property.test.ts, counted rather than estimated. Bounded is pinned by the budget never being exceeded however many candidates exist and by a NaN attempt budget being read as no budget rather than as no bound. Deterministic is pinned by the plan being identical under any permutation of the candidates, of the reported failures, and of both at once, and by exclusions ordered by code point rather than host collation. Observable is pinned by the trail quoting the ENFORCED budget rather than the stated one and by an unattributed rights failure keeping its kind so it cannot be read as a stray timeout.

performance.evidence: npm run bench:failover in packages/media-engine, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree this gate is recorded against. Run separately and deliberately: the one wall-clock assertion is deselected by name in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a performance gate recorded from npm run check would have described the five deterministic read-count assertions and omitted the timed one entirely. This run executes all six -- a bounded number of candidate fields read per candidate at both sizes, no more read per unit of sorted work at 4096 candidates than at 512, a 4096-candidate pool ranked inside the budget a request can afford, a bounded number of failure fields per failure in both shapes and at both sizes, and no greater per-failure cost at 4096 unattributed or attributable failures than at 512.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The implementation predates the claim. packages/media-engine/src/failover.ts opens with Candidate failover (PL-0204), scheduling.ts is the half of it a browser can import, four suites cover it, and vitest.config.ts exists only to keep its wall-clock assertion out of npm run check -- while the task was never claimed and carried no gate results. THE BASE WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN GUESSED, with planFailover and playbackAttemptFailureSchema as behaviour witnesses. The ordering check matters more here than anywhere else: this task spans a contract module and an engine module, so if the contract had landed first then the engine function's parent would sit INSIDE the implementation and the base would be narrowed exactly as PL-0205's was. The runner verified planFailover's introduction is at or before the contract's, took that commit's first parent, and confirmed neither witness appears in source at this base while both appear at HEAD. The media-engine wildcard was narrowed before this run to the nine files this task actually wrote, on the reviewer's rule that allowedPaths is write ownership and that keeping a wildcard because tasks are already serialised is reservation inflation.

review.title: Auth integration decision
review.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS BOTH NARROWED AND WIDENED, AND THE WIDENING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. As declared, this task reserved docs/**, apps/web/src/** and packages/contracts/** -- all twenty-one documents, the entire web application and the whole contracts package -- for a decision record. Each of those three prefix-contains an active task's write surface, so a P0 that is already finished in the tree could not be claimed by anyone. Worse, and in the opposite direction, packages/auth/** was NOT declared at all, yet nine files there are this task's primary output: a reconcile-existing run would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. Both errors come from declaring a surface by guess before the work exists rather than from reading it afterwards. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and only the control-plane record lags, the same pattern as PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0601. All four acceptance clauses are met: packages/auth exports the seam at . and ./server with better-auth a dependency of that package alone; sessions are database-backed through @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts carries ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES with findSurfaceViolations defaulting unknown plugins to violations; and both better-auth and its adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret, asserted by enabled-surface.test.ts against REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. The decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md, which self-labels Proposed because claude-lead wrote it and WAS also this task's reviewAgent when it was written -- that is no longer true, see the reviewAgent change below, and the label should be revisited by whoever closes this task. TWO HONEST CAVEATS STATED IN THE ADR RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and neither is an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed against a database, because there is no PostgreSQL anywhere in this environment; and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. PROVENANCE: this must be started with --reconcile-existing, not against HEAD. The probe is packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts -- but after the PL-0205 finding, a filename probe is not enough on its own: whoever reconciles it must confirm the candidate base tree contains neither ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES nor WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES anywhere, so a file created by a later move cannot open the range after the behaviour it claims to cover. REVIEWAGENT MOVED FROM claude-lead TO gpt-architect. This task carries a security-review gate on an authentication boundary, and its decision record was written by claude-lead. A reviewer that is also the author is not a reviewer; routing it outward makes the review stricter rather than looser, which is the only direction this may be changed in. THE MIGRATION IS A REVIEWDEPENDENCY, AND THE REVIEWER MADE THAT A CONDITION OF CLAIMING. It observed that this record cites packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql as the factual basis for the database-backed-session clause while the file sat in no part of the declared surface, and gave two defensible resolutions and one forbidden one: add it as a reviewDependency, or stop using it as evidence and let the Drizzle adapter and configuration carry the clause alone -- but do not mix the two. Its words: either is defensible; mixing the two is not. Resolved as a reviewDependency, because the ADR genuinely does rest on it: ADR-007 argues database-backed sessions over stateless ones partly on the shape of that migration, and an approval that did not fingerprint it could stay fresh after the schema underneath the argument changed. It is deliberately NOT an allowedPath -- this task did not write it, PL-0402 did, and reviewDependencies exist precisely so a boundary a task depends on can be reviewed without being reserved. No collision follows: reviewDependencies reserve nothing, so PL-0402 may still declare packages/persistence/** as a write surface whenever it is claimed.
review.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The implementation predates the claim. packages/auth holds nine source files, better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned there at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret range, enabled-surface.ts declares the permitted capabilities and the withheld plugin families, and the decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md -- while the task was never claimed and carried no gate results. THE BASE WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN GUESSED, on the same rule and by the same five checks as PL-0601, using ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES as behaviour witnesses. The declared surface was corrected in BOTH directions before this run: narrowed from docs and apps and contracts wildcards that between them reserved most of the repository, and widened to packages/auth, which the task had never declared despite that package being its primary output -- so a reconcile against the old declaration would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. The migration ADR-007 rests on is a reviewDependency rather than a write path, on the reviewer's instruction that citing it as evidence while leaving it outside the surface was the one unacceptable option.

review.title: Channel and EPG contracts
review.notes: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE, ONLY THE RECORD LAGS -- the fourth task found in this state, after PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0401. packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts is a 592-line contract module whose header names this task, live.test.ts is 686 lines with fast-check property suites, and docs/LIVE_TV.md is a 239-line rewrite around it. All four required contracts exist as real schemas rather than stubs: liveChannelSchema, epgListingSchema, epgWindowSchema and epgScheduleSchema, with epgInstantSchema and the XMLTV timestamp reader beneath them and compareEpgListings, sortEpgListings and sortEpgSchedule for deterministic ordering. THE RIGHTS DIMENSION HOLDS, which matters because this task carries a rights-review gate. A channel's rights basis is REQUIRED and non-nullable, deliberately unlike a title's, and it uses the one shared contentRightsSchema rather than restating the values. No media address or stream URL can appear in a channel or listing: liveChannelSchema declares none, and epgListingSchema is protected three ways -- a PLAYABILITY_BEARING_KEYS list, a CarriesNoPlayability conditional type with a compile-time witness, and .strict() so a feed sending streamUrl is refused rather than silently stripped. rightsBasisForListing refuses a listing that names another channel with a distinguishable reason instead of answering null. The opaque rights reference is not here at all, by design: the live contract carries only the category, and the reference half lives in the provider layer where it is shape-validated and never parsed. logoUrl is the single URL-typed field and is branding rather than media, deliberately absent from PLAYABILITY_BEARING_KEYS. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED FROM packages/contracts/**, which prefix-contained PL-0706's leaf and PL-0207's, to the four files this task actually wrote -- the contract, its suite, its document, and the one assertion in module-boundary.test.ts that had to be retired because it previously asserted src/domains/live.ts must NOT exist. That retirement is this task's edit and is declared rather than left outside every surface. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md is DROPPED: it has no live section, only two bullets under Planned contracts naming /api/v1/live/channels and /api/v1/live/epg, and docs/LIVE_TV.md states the policy that API_CONTRACTS gains live routes when a live route exists. This task defines no HTTP route shapes; those are PL-0602's. Nothing here needs packages/contracts/package.json or index.ts either, because the exports wildcard resolves a new domain module with no metadata edit and the barrel does not re-export live. PREFERREDAGENT MOVED FROM gpt-architect TO claude-media, and this is a correction of fact rather than a reassignment: the implementation in the tree was written in this lane, so recording it as the external agent's would be a false provenance claim. The reviewer stays gpt-architect. PROVENANCE: start with --reconcile-existing. The probe is packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts, and the PL-0205 lesson applies -- confirm the candidate base tree contains no liveChannelSchema or epgListingSchema anywhere before trusting the file's creation date, because a file created by a later refactor opens the range after the behaviour it claims to cover.
review.acceptance: Licensed channel, program, schedule, and EPG contracts are typed and documented

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck via npm run check, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree this gate is recorded against. The live contract compiles as a leaf under the contracts module boundary: it imports only zod, shared/ids and shared/rights, and the CarriesNoPlayability conditional type resolves against a compile-time witness, so a listing that gained a playability-bearing key would fail to typecheck rather than fail a test.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The implementation predates the claim. packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts is a complete contract module whose header names this task, live.test.ts is its suite, and docs/LIVE_TV.md is written around it -- while the task was never claimed and carried no gate results. THE BASE WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN GUESSED, on the rule the reviewer stated after PL-0205: prove the behaviour was absent before the base and present because of the implementation, and never substitute the creation date of the file that happens to contain it today. Two behaviour witnesses were used, liveChannelSchema and epgListingSchema, located with git log --reverse and the pickaxe over packages and apps, which reports where a symbol first appears anywhere in source and is therefore immune to a later refactor moving it between files. The runner verified that the liveChannelSchema introduction is at or before the epgListingSchema introduction, so the first marker really is the boundary; that this base is that commit's first parent, resolved with rev-parse --verify; that neither witness appears in source at this base, each asserted on an exact no-match exit code rather than merely a non-zero one; and that HEAD still carries them. It also self-tested the probe itself first, against a marker whose introduction commit was already known, because an earlier run produced three refusals that turned out to mean only that the command was broken.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
recommended.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
recommended.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.
